Hi Jules / Asha — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed trial plan so we have aligned success criteria and owners before we kick off the sandbox: 

TL;DR: Redwood will provision a 2-week trial environment (dedicated tenant + streaming endpoints) and deliver an SDK sample, agreed evaluation prompts, and a short acceptance checklist. GridPay will validate 3 success criteria and nominate an engineer to integrate the streaming client.

What we covered on the call (high level):
- Trial goal: reduce fraud review latency and increase automated classification recall on payment disputes.
- Target integration: server-side streaming via Redwood Streaming API for real-time token-by-token evaluation + tool-calling for downstream lookups.
- Success criteria: latency < 120ms per token tail, classification F1 >= 0.78 on the agreed sample, and acceptable cost per 1k tokens.

Proposed mutual action plan (first pass):
1) Redwood: provision trial tenant + API keys, provide SDK streaming sample and tool-calling example (owner: Dev). ETA: 2027-04-15.
2) GridPay: provide a 3000-record evaluation set (anonymized) and nominate integration lead (owner: Asha). ETA: 2027-04-13.
3) Joint: verify baseline metrics on day 1 and schedule a mid-trial checkpoint (owner: Connor). ETA: 2027-04-19.
4) Final review & acceptance: run the evaluation harness, review cost/latency, and decide next steps (owner: Jules + Connor). ETA: 2027-04-25.

Integration notes we discussed:
- SDK: we recommend the Node streaming client for your eventing system; sample shows token streaming + on-the-fly tool-calls to internal lookup service.
- API routes: /v1/stream/generate for streaming tokens, /v1/exec/tool for synchronous tool calls; we will give explicit route examples in the sample.
- Auth: scoped API key + optional mTLS for Private mode.

Attachments: gridpay-poc-success-criteria.xlsx (draft) and connor_gridpay_sdk-integration-snippet.patch (streaming sample diff).

Next steps from me: I will share the provisional tenant details and push the SDK snippet to the GitHub sandbox by Thursday (04/15). Can you confirm who on your side will be the integration lead and share the anonymized eval dataset by 04/13?

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—Connor
